metadata.design: One-word English animal names, each given alone as the user message with a space first (" lion"). A name that splits into several tokens is read at its last token, and its token count is recorded. The label is the animal's group (8), which follows from its class in the Catalogue of Life. Each animal also carries its way of life (habitat, how it moves, diet, wild or domestic) and, apart from its categories, its taxonomy (the accepted name and rank, phylum, class, order, family, genus). Orders are the families held out whole in validation. Some animals' kinship and way of life disagree (whales, bats, penguins, starfish), so the lens can show which the model follows.

groups.label: mammal
groups.description: Mammals, the class Mammalia: cats, dogs and their kin, primates, rodents, hoofed animals, whales, bats, marsupials and monotremes

groups.label: bird
groups.description: Birds, the class Aves: birds of prey, crows and songbirds, pigeons, parrots, waterbirds, shorebirds and seabirds, game birds, and the flightless birds

groups.label: reptile
groups.description: Reptiles, the class Reptilia: snakes, lizards, turtles and tortoises, crocodilians and the tuatara

groups.label: amphibian
groups.description: Amphibians, the class Amphibia: frogs and toads, salamanders and newts, and caecilians

groups.label: fish
groups.description: Fishes, every vertebrate outside the four classes of land vertebrates: sharks and rays, ray-finned fishes, sturgeons and gars, lampreys, hagfishes, lungfishes and the coelacanth

groups.label: insect
groups.description: Insects, the class Insecta: beetles, butterflies and moths, bees, ants and wasps, flies, true bugs, grasshoppers, dragonflies and smaller orders

groups.label: arachnid
groups.description: Arachnids, the class Arachnida: spiders, scorpions, harvestmen, mites and their kin

groups.label: other_invertebrate
groups.description: Every other animal: molluscs, crustaceans, centipedes and millipedes, springtails, segmented worms, roundworms and flatworms, jellyfish and corals, and echinoderms
